headline: Bank of England Raises Interest Rate to 4% in First Hike in Over Three Years
summary: The Bank of England raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter point to 4% in its first rate increase in over three years, responding to soaring global energy costs and inflation.
why: Central bank interest rate hikes are primary monetary policy tools used to combat inflation by increasing borrowing costs across the economy.

impacts.name: British Pound
impacts.why: Interest rate hikes generally strengthen currency demand by increasing yields on domestic fixed-income assets.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: A surprise quarter-point rate increase by the central bank tightened monetary policy in response to energy-driven inflation pressures.
